clue.text: Stars may have a share

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase: the thing that may have a share

blocks.note: first meaning: the group of seven bright stars in Ursa Major, so named in Britain
second meaning: the farm implement whose cutting blade is called its share

explanation.surface: Celebrities may get a cut of the profits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Share' looks like money but is the ploughshare, the blade; Britons call the Big Dipper the Plough.
explanation.definitionFit: The constellation known in America as the Big Dipper takes this name in Britain, and the farm tool carries a blade called a share.

clue.text: Risk supporting rising Republican, maybe

indicators.note: in a down answer rising means going up the page, the reverse order
in a down answer the supporting word sits below the other

blocks.note: Rep is a short form of Republican
a chance is a risk

explanation.surface: Danger props up a Republican on the way up.
explanation.definitionFit: The old-fashioned adverb means possibly or perhaps, the same as maybe.

clue.text: Trees we see round mountains

blocks.note: O is round in shape
ranges of mountains

explanation.surface: Forests surround the peaks.
explanation.definitionFit: The citrus fruit gives its name to the evergreen trees that bear it.

clue.text: Septimus Harding, perhaps, willing to supervise wild life?

blocks.note: game means willing, as in game for anything
the hero of Trollope's novel The Warden, an almshouse warden

explanation.surface: Trollope's gentle cleric is ready to look after animals.
explanation.walkthrough: Septimus Harding is the warden of Hiram's Hospital in Trollope's The Warden; 'perhaps' marks him as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: This officer is employed to protect game animals on an estate or reserve, the wild life of the clue.

clue.text: Articles name Scotsman as Theseus's fellow citizen

blocks.note: the two articles, the indefinite and the definite
N is the abbreviation for name
a typical Scottish first name

explanation.surface: Some grammar items label a man from Scotland as a compatriot of the Greek hero.
explanation.definitionFit: Theseus was the legendary king of Athens, so anyone sharing his city was a citizen of Athens.

clue.text: Entertainer can depart in disorder

indicators.note: in disorder means jumbled, so the letters are mixed up

blocks.note: the letters as printed

explanation.surface: A performer can leave in a hurry and a mess.
explanation.definitionFit: A stage performer who dances in shoes with metal plates is one kind of entertainer.

clue.text: Artist portraying pier? Not at first

indicators.note: not at first says the opening letter is absent

blocks.note: a jetty is a pier

explanation.surface: A painter depicting a jetty.
explanation.walkthrough: William Etty was a Victorian painter famous for nudes.
explanation.definitionFit: William Etty, the nineteenth-century English painter from York, is a crossword favourite among painters.

clue.text: Occupy a brother thus attired -

definitions.note: a phrase reading as in habit

blocks.note: first meaning: to live in
second meaning: a monk wearing his robe is in his habit

explanation.walkthrough: A brother here is a friar or monk, whose robe is called a habit.
explanation.definitionFit: To live in a place is to occupy it, and a monk dressed in his robe is in habit.

clue.text: The shark is large but tender

blocks.note: first meaning: a large sluggish shark of warm seas
second meaning: one who looks after the sick

explanation.surface: That big fish is surprisingly gentle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tender' reads as an adjective, soft, but it is a noun: one who tends.
explanation.definitionFit: A hospital carer tends patients, and the bottom-dwelling shark species of warm waters shares the name.

clue.text: River effluent initially confined by agent

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter only
confined by means held inside the following word

blocks.note: a secret agent
its first letter

explanation.surface: An agent keeps sewage out of a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Spey is a Scottish salmon river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spey is a fast-flowing river in the Scottish Highlands, famous for salmon fishing and whisky distilleries.

clue.text: Way scholar quietly makes a regional plan

blocks.note: a road is a way
a Master of Arts, a graduate scholar
p, piano, the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: An academic working without fuss draws up a plan for a district.
explanation.definitionFit: A chart of the routes through an area is literally a plan of the region, used to find the way about.

clue.text: Vessel whose motion makes us seasick

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for the ship

blocks.note: first meaning: a jug for pouring
second meaning: a ship that rises and falls bow and stern in heavy seas

explanation.surface: A boat whose rolling turns the passengers green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' and the seasickness both seem to describe one ship; the first is in fact a jug.
explanation.definitionFit: A jug for water is a kind of container, and a ship that plunges up and down in waves is said to pitch.

clue.text: But no lofty method was adopted by this robber

definitions.text: But no lofty method was adopted by this robber

blocks.clueFragment: But no lofty method was adopted by this robber
blocks.note: surface reading: a thief who did not take the moral high road
setter's reading: lofty is high and a method is a way, so this robber's very name is built on a high way

explanation.surface: A villain who never chose the noble course.
explanation.definitionFit: The mounted robber of old held up coaches on main public roads, which were called the king's high roads.

clue.text: Legally qualified for this sort of rating?

blocks.note: first meaning: having the legal competence to act
second meaning: the naval grade of seaman abbreviated AB

explanation.walkthrough: A rating is an ordinary sailor in the Royal Navy, and one grade is the able seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: Lawyers speak of a person being competent in law, and the Navy ranks a trained sailor as an able seaman.

clue.text: Look on BR employee as a bucolic type

blocks.note: to count someone a friend is to look on them as one
RY is railway, and a man is an employee; BR was British Rail

explanation.surface: Regard a British Rail worker as a rustic.
explanation.walkthrough: BR was British Rail, the state railway of the time.
explanation.definitionFit: Bucolic means rustic, and a person who lives in rural parts rather than town is a rural sort.

clue.text: Scheme to stop careless play

blocks.note: no as a cry to make someone stop
to strum is to play a guitar idly

explanation.surface: A plan to put an end to sloppy performances.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a favourite remedy or pet plan for setting things right, often a quack one.

clue.text: Element from the boundaries of Manhattan

definitions.text: Element from the boundaries of Manhattan

blocks.clueFragment: Element from the boundaries of Manhattan
blocks.note: surface reading: some feature found along the edges of the New York borough
setter's reading: the outer letters of Manhattan, M and N, together form the chemical symbol of a metallic element

explanation.surface: Something found at the edges of New York's island borough.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue does not build the word letter by letter: it gives the symbol Mn, and the solver names the element it stands for.
explanation.definitionFit: Mn is the periodic-table symbol of the grey brittle metal with atomic number 25, used in making steel.

clue.text: Scottish tenant is a cert for being thrown out

indicators.note: something thrown out is tossed about, so the letters land in a new order

blocks.note: the letters as printed

explanation.surface: A Highland tenant is sure to be evicted.
explanation.walkthrough: The Highland Clearances evicted many such tenants, which gives the surface its sting.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the holder of a croft, a small rented farm in the Scottish Highlands and islands.

clue.text: Eden's 25 adapted for us to 7?

indicators.note: adapted means altered, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
the answer to 25 down

explanation.surface: A cross-reference riddle about adapting Eden's dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 7 is inhabit, so the definition reads 'for us to inhabit'.
explanation.definitionFit: A house or home is somewhere for people to live in, which is what the cross-reference describes.

clue.text: Egyptian has a firm in the Orient, perhaps

blocks.note: the Orient is the East, abbreviated E
taken as written
firm in the sense of strict

explanation.surface: A man from Cairo runs a company somewhere in Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' marks Egyptian as one example of the definition; 'firm' is not a company but means strict.
explanation.definitionFit: Egypt lies in the Near East, so an Egyptian thing can be described as belonging to the Orient.

clue.text: Dismiss objection to an old instrument

blocks.note: to sack is to fire
a but is an objection, as in no ifs or buts

explanation.surface: Fire someone for complaining about an antique.
explanation.definitionFit: This medieval and Renaissance brass wind with a slide was the forerunner of the trombone.

clue.text: No way for aliens to become park keepers

indicators.note: no means without, so the named piece is taken away

blocks.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
aliens are outsiders

explanation.surface: Foreigners have no route into the job of looking after parks.
explanation.definitionFit: Wardens who patrol and look after national parks and forests carry this title.

clue.text: A king with endless duties somehow to be learned

indicators.note: endless means losing the end, so the final letter goes
somehow means in some unspecified way, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: Edward Rex, the royal cipher of a king Edward
taken as written

explanation.surface: A monarch with endless obligations has to study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Learned' looks like a verb but is the adjective, pronounced in two syllables.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone very well read and scholarly is learned, showing great knowledge gained from study.

clue.text: Endearing character unpopular with certain sportsmen

blocks.note: first meaning: Donald, the lovable cartoon bird
second meaning: a score of nothing, which no cricketer wants

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a batsman out without scoring has made a duck, nought being shaped like an egg.
explanation.definitionFit: The Disney cartoon bird is a lovable figure, and a zero score is what batsmen dread.

clue.text: Have visions of a wee drop outside Gravesend

indicators.note: outside means wrapped around the next piece, which sits within

blocks.note: a small measure of whisky
the Kent town read as grave's end, the last letter of grave

explanation.surface: Seeing things after a whisky near a Kent town.
explanation.walkthrough: Gravesend is a town on the Thames in Kent; split it as grave's end to get one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To see images in sleep, or to imagine wishfully, is to have visions.

clue.text: Not a bad reason for supporting an exhibition site

blocks.note: fair means not bad, middling
a ground is a reason, as in grounds for complaint

explanation.surface: A decent justification for backing something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For supporting' just joins the pieces; the definition is the last two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Shows, funfairs and agricultural exhibitions are held on an open field set aside for them.

clue.text: Sort of pudding portion Eric eats

indicators.note: a portion is a part, so the letters lie within the next words

blocks.note: found across the two words

explanation.surface: A dessert that a boy called Eric tucks into.
explanation.definitionFit: Grains boiled slowly in sweetened milk make a classic British baked milk pudding.

clue.text: Fashionable support for state growth

indicators.note: in a down answer the support sits beneath what it holds up

blocks.note: Georgia, the US state
in fashion

explanation.surface: Trendy backing for national expansion.
explanation.definitionFit: An increase in size or amount is an addition, as when one puts on weight.

clue.text: Include a doctor in 19 stock

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the doctor goes within the other pieces

blocks.note: Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree
the answer to 19, eastern, abbreviated
stock in the sense of lineage

explanation.surface: Take in a medic as part of the eastern stock.
explanation.walkthrough: The doctor goes into the gap between the abbreviation for 19 and the word for stock.
explanation.definitionFit: To embrace a range of topics is to take them all in, so the verb means to comprise.

clue.text: He wrote verses about a member no one returned

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so these words are read from the end

blocks.note: c, circa, about
taken as written
a Member of Parliament
no, then one as the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A poet wrote lines about an MP nobody voted back in.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Campion was an Elizabethan poet and composer of lute songs. 'Returned' plays on electing an MP.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Campion, the Elizabethan lyricist, set his own poems to music, so he is a writer of verse.

clue.text: Greek character can always be a rebel

blocks.note: a letter of the Greek alphabet
a tin is a can
e'er, the poetic contraction of ever

explanation.surface: A Greek person can never stop being a rebel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' means a letter, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: One who rises against authority, especially sailors against their captain, is a mutinous insurgent.

clue.text: Explosive noise for which a Duchess's son got beaten

definitions.text: Explosive noise for which a Duchess's son got beaten

blocks.note: surface reading: a bang, a blast
setter's reading: in Alice in Wonderland the Duchess sings that her baby boy should be beaten whenever he does it

explanation.surface: An aristocrat's boy is thrashed for a bang.
explanation.walkthrough: The Duchess's lullaby runs: 'Speak roughly to your little boy, and beat him when he' does this, because he only does it to annoy.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden violent expulsion of air through the nose is a loud bursting sound, the act the lullaby punishes.
